merger_description:
Peter Warren Automotive Holdings Ltd (Peter Warren) proposes to acquire:

* 100% of the shares of Paul Wakeling Motor Group Pty Ltd;
* 100% of the shares of Wollongong City Motors Pty Ltd; and
* the business and trading net assets of Hurrikayne Pty Ltd, relating to the Moss Vale Motor Group

from Wakeling Automotive Group (Wakeling Automotive) (the Acquisition), as part of which Peter Warren will acquire 30 new and used car dealerships in New South Wales.

Peter Warren is an ASX-listed new and used car retailing business that operates over 80 automotive dealership sites at 25 locations across the east coast of Australia. Peter Warren represents 30 Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) vehicle brands as an authorised dealer, and also supplies OEM spare parts and aftermarket vehicle servicing.

Wakeling Automotive is a new and used car retailing business that operates 30 automotive dealership sites at 8 locations across Sydney, Wollongong and the Southern Highlands. Wakeling Automotive represents 16 OEM vehicle brands as an authorised dealer, and also supplies OEM spare parts and aftermarket vehicle servicing.

Both Peter Warren and Wakeling Automotive supply new and used cars, OEM spare parts and aftermarket vehicle servicing in the Campbelltown/Narellan/Smeaton Grange suburbs of southern Sydney.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the interests of consumers.

Where the ACCC is satisfied that the acquisition, if put into effect, could, in all the circumstances, have the effect of substantially lessening competition in a market, the ACCC may also consider whether any competition issues can be addressed by one or more conditions.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines and interim merger process guidelines.

In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered the information and documents that were submitted with the notification form, additional information provided by the parties to the Acquisition, market feedback and publicly available information.
For the reasons given below, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into effect with conditions.
Overlap between the Parties
Peter Warren and Wakeling Automotive (the Parties) overlap in the retail supply of:

items: OEM spare parts, and car servicing and repairs

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The Parties’ dealership sites overlap on a local basis in the Campbelltown, Narellan, and Smeaton Grange suburbs located in the Macarthur region,2 south-west of Sydney. 2 The Macarthur region includes Campbelltown, Smeaton Grange and Narellan and the immediate surrounding suburbs. Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028)
Within this region, Peter Warren operates 13 dealership sites across 2 locations:

items: 7 dealership sites in Campbelltown: Nissan, LDV, MG, Mazda, Ford, Jaguar & Land Rover and Mercedes Benz.
6 dealership sites in Narellan: Ford, Honda, Omoda Jaecoo, Geely, Kia and Suzuki.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Within this region, Wakeling Automotive operates 12 dealership sites across 3 locations:

items: 7 dealership sites in Campbelltown: Hyundai, RAM, Kia, GMSV, Mitsubishi, Isuzu UTE and Volkswagen.
4 dealership sites in Smeaton Grange: GWM/Haval, Mitsubishi, Hyundai and Isuzu UTE.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: In these locations, the Parties overlap in the supply of the Kia brand. Peter Warren also owns a Kia dealership site in Warwick Farm in southern Sydney.
The Parties provide OEM spare sparts and car servicing and repairs for all of these car dealership sites.
Industry background
There are over 3,000 car dealership sites in Australia, comprising large and small dealership chains as well as independent dealerships.
The new car retailing supply chain generally includes:

items: Upstream car manufacturers, which manufacture vehicles and OEM spare parts overseas.
Australian-based OEM distributors, which are subsidiaries of car manufacturers, and act as links between the car manufacturer and the Australian authorised dealer network.
New car authorised dealers, which enter into agreements with OEMs to sell new cars and provide servicing and repairs.
Independent mechanics or repairers, which repair or service cars.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: Although OEMs typically set recommended retail prices (RRPs) for new cars, discounting off the RRP is prevalent in the automotive industry. Dealerships also compete on non-price factors to attract customers, such as customer service, location, stock availability, delivery times, and extras.

New car dealership sites also typically supply OEM spare parts, servicing and repairs. New cars generally have a warranty period of around 5 years, although this can vary, Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028) and OEMs often offer free or capped price servicing for a period. Authorised dealership sites carry out servicing and repairs on behalf of OEMs.

The ACCC’s view is that most new car buyers service their car at an authorised dealership service centre during the warranty period and any free or capped price servicing period. The use of independent repairers for repairs and servicing increases significantly as these periods near expiry. 3. Competition assessment

The ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the continuation of the current state of competition (being the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed).
Relevant areas of competition
The ACCC considers the relevant areas of competitive overlap for the purposes of its assessment are the supply of:

items: new cars to retail customers in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas
servicing and repairs of Kia cars in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: While the Parties also overlap in the retail supply of OEM spare parts, used cars and vehicle insurance and finance products, the ACCC does not consider the Acquisition is likely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in these markets. This is because Peter Warren is likely to continue to face competition from alternative suppliers of these products and services.
This determination does not consider these overlaps further. Supply of new cars to retail customers in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas

The ACCC considers that the supply of new and used cars occurs in separate markets. Most used car dealerships that exclusively sell used cars are not authorised by OEMs to sell new cars. While there may be some substitutability between very low- mileage used cars and new cars, the ACCC considers new and used cars are generally not close substitutes, and competitive dynamics between the supply of new and used cars differ, given that for used cars there is competition from used car dealerships and online sales.3

For the supply of new cars, the ACCC considers that there is both inter- and intra- brand competition between dealership sites. Inter-brand competition is competition between sellers of different OEM brands, while intra-brand competition is competition between different sellers of the same OEM brand.

Market feedback and industry reports indicate that many buyers typically decide on an OEM brand and model before visiting a dealership. The ACCC therefore considers that intra-band competition between car dealership sites of the same OEM brand is 3 The ACCC considered these issues in the AP Eagers Limited / Automotive Holdings Group Limited Determination. Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028) likely to exert the strongest competitive constraint at a retail level. However, for some customers, inter-brand competition is also relevant, particularly between OEM brands offering similar categories of vehicles, with similar prices and key features.

In assessing the Acquisition, the ACCC has considered the effects on intra-brand competition, noting the Parties overlap in relation to the supply of new Kia cars, as well as inter-brand competition, given the range of OEM brands offered by the Parties.

Based on information before it, the ACCC also considers that the supply of new cars to retail customers (individual consumers) and the supply of new cars to commercial customers (fleet customers) occur in separate product markets, given fleet customers tend to be able to source cars from a wider geographic area than retail customers. Therefore, in assessing the Acquisition, the ACCC has focused on the supply of new cars to retail customers.

The Parties made submissions defining the geographic market for the supply of new cars as an area extending at least 40km (straight line) from the Parties’ dealerships in the Macarthur region. Market feedback indicated that some customers may be prepared to travel greater distances to purchase a new car, although some may prefer to buy locally having regard to servicing considerations.
The ACCC considers that information before it indicates that most customers prefer to purchase a new car from a dealer in their local region close to where they live.

The ACCC has also considered the constraint posed by dealership sites in southern Sydney and Wollongong in the competitive assessment below. Based on the materials before it, the ACCC considers that the constraint one dealership site poses on another dealership site weakens the further away they are located from each other.

The ACCC therefore considers that the relevant geographic market for the supply of new cars to retail customers is the Macarthur region and surrounding areas. Supply of servicing and repairs of Kia cars in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas

Third party feedback indicates that during any capped price servicing and warranty periods, the supply of servicing and repairs is segmented by OEM brand. This is because warranty and capped price servicing is generally only available at dealership sites authorised to service the relevant OEM brand. The ACCC considers that independent repairers are likely to become more of a competitive constraint as these periods near expiry.

In assessing the Acquisition, the ACCC has focused on the Parties’ overlapping OEM brand, Kia. In this respect, the ACCC’s primary focus has been on Wakeling Automotive’s Kia dealership service centre in Campbelltown and Peter Warren’s Kia dealership service centres in Narellan and Warwick Farm.

The Parties provided submissions that for most dealerships in the Macarthur region, during the initial few years from purchase, customers return to have their car serviced at the service centre where they purchased the car, however this changes over time.

Based on the information before it, including third party feedback, the ACCC considers that consumers prefer to service their car at service centres located close Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028) to where they live or work. Given the frequency of servicing and repairs, consumers are typically less willing to travel than they are when purchasing a new car.
The ACCC therefore considers that the relevant geographic area for the supply of servicing and repairs of Kia cars is the Macarthur region and surrounding areas.
Competition effects in the supply of new cars to retail customers in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas

The ACCC is satisfied that, disregarding any conditions the ACCC could include, the Acquisition could, in all the circumstances, have the effect, or likely effect, of substantially lessening competition in the supply of new cars to retail customers in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas.

If put into effect, the Acquisition would combine the 2 largest suppliers of new cars to retail customers in the Macarthur region, and Peter Warren would operate 25 out of 34 dealership sites.4 The Acquisition would therefore materially increase concentration in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas. In addition, the Acquisition could significantly reduce the competitive constraint on Peter Warren by removing competition between Peter Warren and Wakeling Automotive.

The ACCC considers that the Parties are close competitors in relation to the supply of new cars in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas and they compete closely on both price and non-price factors for customers. Information before the ACCC indicates that the customer catchment areas of the Parties’ dealership sites overlap.

On an intra-brand basis, the Parties operate the only Kia dealership sites in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas. The Parties’ sites are in close proximity, with Peter Warren’s Kia site in Narellan and Wakeling Automotive’s Kia site in Campbelltown being within 15 minutes’ driving distance.

On an inter-brand basis, the ACCC considers that the Parties are close competitors in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas, supplying similar categories of OEM brands. For example, the Parties have dealership sites in close proximity which supply high-volume OEM brands with similar model types and price points, such as Ford, GWM, Mazda, Hyundai, Kia, MG and Chery.

The ACCC considers that if the Acquisition were put into effect, Peter Warren would likely continue to face some competitive constraint from other dealership sites in the Macarthur region. However, there would only be 9 remaining competing dealership sites owned by 5 different operators post-Acquisition, and these sites would not provide any intra-brand constraint, given they do not supply any of the same OEM brands as the Parties.

As outlined above, the ACCC considers that competing dealership sites located in southern Sydney and Wollongong would likely provide a weak constraint, due to consumers typically purchasing new cars close to where they live. However, for the reasons expressed above and based on materials before it, the ACCC considers that 4 The ACCC understands that since the Phase 2 Notice for Peter Warren / Wakeling Automotive (MN-30002) was published on 2 June 2026, a new entrant has established a dealership site in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas, increasing the total number of dealership sites from 33 to 34. Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028) dealerships in those areas may provide a more meaningful constraint for the Parties’ customers who live closer to these dealerships.

Based on its experience in previous matters5 and third-party feedback obtained in relation to this matter, the ACCC considers that dealership sites located outside the Macarthur region and surrounding areas are unlikely to provide a sufficient constraint through online, email, and telephone inquiries. This is because there is limited price transparency during these inquiries and dealership sites tend to provide their best discounts only in person.

The ACCC also considered whether OEM volume incentives and other remuneration incentives for individual dealership sites would be likely to constrain Peter Warren post-Acquisition. While these incentives may encourage dealership sites to achieve sales targets and compete for new car sales, the ACCC considers that they may be unlikely to prevent Peter Warren from raising prices across its Macarthur dealership sites. As Peter Warren would own the majority of the new car dealerships in the region (including the only 2 Kia dealership sites and a strong representation of high- volume brands), the Acquisition could give it the ability and incentive to raise prices across its dealerships without substantially reducing its volumes. Further, since the ACCC considers that there is limited price transparency in relation to new car sales, customers may be unlikely to detect a price rise across Peter Warren’s dealerships. The ACCC considers that due to the difficulties in determining the best available price for a particular car, a price increase may be likely to have limited impact on demand and total volumes.

The ACCC was advised that a new Macarthur Mahindra dealership site opened in 2026 in the Macarthur region. However, the ACCC considers that the new Mahindra dealership site is likely to provide a limited constraint on the Parties post-acquisition based on it only being one new site. The ACCC also considers there is a low likelihood of additional timely new entry or expansion at sufficient scale to replace the reduction in competition likely to result from the Acquisition. Market feedback indicates that barriers to entry and expansion are likely to be high, given limited access to quality sites in locations where most OEM brands are already present. While the ACCC considers small-scale entry may occur, this would be unlikely to replace the loss of competition caused by the Acquisition.

Having regard to the combination of factors identified above, the ACCC considers, absent any condition the ACCC could include, the Acquisition could have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the supply of new cars to retail customers in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas.
Competition effects in the supply of servicing and repairs of Kia cars in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas

The ACCC is satisfied that, disregarding any conditions the ACCC could include, the Acquisition could, in all the circumstances, have the effect, or likely effect, of substantially lessening competition in the supply of servicing and repairs of Kia cars in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas.

Given the geographic proximity between the Parties’ Kia dealership service centres, the ACCC considers that the Parties are likely each other’s closest competitors in the 5 For example, AP Eagers Limited / Automotive Holdings Group Limited Determination, paragraph 6.27. Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028) supply of Kia servicing and repairs. The Acquisition, if put into effect, would remove this competition. Peter Warren would operate the only Kia dealership service centres in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas, as well as the Kia dealership service centre in Warwick Farm.

The ACCC considers that post-Acquisition, Peter Warren would be unlikely to face sufficient constraint from competing Kia dealership sites during any capped price servicing or warranty periods. This is because the next closest Kia dealership service centres are located in southern Sydney. During these periods, the ACCC considers independent repairers in the Macarthur region are unlikely to provide a sufficient constraint, although they are likely to become a stronger constraint outside the capped price servicing period or towards the end of the warranty period.

Having regard to the combination of factors identified above, the ACCC considers, absent any condition, the Acquisition could have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the market for the supply of servicing and repairs of Kia cars in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas. 4. Conditions
The ACCC has determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Act that the Acquisition may be put into effect, subject to conditions.

The conditions are: 1. Peter Warren must divest, or cause the divestiture of, the Divestiture Business to a purchaser approved in writing by the ACCC in accordance with a section 87B undertaking accepted by the ACCC. 2. Peter Warren must provide the ACCC with an executed undertaking under section 87B of the Act in respect of the divestiture of the Divestiture Business, in the form at Attachment A of this determination, within five business days of the date of this determination and comply with that undertaking. (together, the Conditions).
The term Divestiture Business is defined in the section 87B undertaking that Peter Warren must give and comply with pursuant to the Conditions.

In summary, the Divestiture Business comprises all the assets and operations of 8 dealerships at specified sites and associated service centres (including a Kia dealership site and service centre) at two locations in the Macarthur region at Smeaton Grange and Campbelltown in NSW.

The ACCC must not include conditions unless it is satisfied that, disregarding any conditions the ACCC could include, the Acquisition, if put into effect, could, in all the circumstances, have the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market.

The ACCC must have regard to all relevant matters, and may have regard to the effect on the interests of consumers that compliance with the conditions would have, or be likely to have, or any consumer benefits that would result, or be likely to result from compliance with the conditions. Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028)

It is a contravention of section 45AZ of the Act for a person to put the Acquisition into effect and to not comply with any conditions. Where a person does not comply with conditions, the Federal Court may make orders including, in some circumstances, divestiture or a declaration that the Acquisition is void.
Assessment with the Conditions

As set out above, the ACCC is satisfied that, disregarding any conditions the ACCC could include, the Acquisition could, in all the circumstances, have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the supply of new cars to retail customers and the supply of servicing and repairs of Kia cars in the Macarthur region and surrounding areas. To address this, the ACCC has decided to include the Conditions in its determination.
The objective of the Conditions is to address the competition issues identified in respect of the Acquisition, as set out in this determination and statement of reasons.
The conditions incorporate a remedy offer Peter Warren proposed to the ACCC on 13 July 2026, with revisions.
The Conditions address the competition issues

The Conditions address the competition issues set out above by preserving the presence in the relevant markets of an independent supplier and a sufficient level of competitive constraint that would otherwise be lost as a result of the Acquisition by facilitating the entry or expansion of a competitor through divestiture to a purchaser approved by the ACCC.
The Conditions can be effectively implemented

The ACCC has also had regard to whether there are risks associated with implementation that would limit the effectiveness of the Conditions in addressing the competition issues. The ACCC considers that the Conditions can be effectively implemented. Composition of the Divestiture Business

The ACCC considers that the Divestiture Business will be appropriately configured by the end of the Initial Sales Period and that a suitable purchaser may operate it effectively. The ACCC has had regard to third party feedback in reaching this view, as well as the nature and terms of the Conditions and the undertaking. Emergence of an appropriate purchaser

Based on submissions provided by Peter Warren and third-party feedback, the ACCC considers there are suitable purchasers available to support a timely and effective divestiture to an ACCC-approved purchaser. Determination | Peter Warren – Wakeling Automotive (MN - 90028) Integrity of the Divestiture Business and other considerations

The ACCC considers that the integrity of the Divestiture Business will be protected prior to divestiture, and took account of other considerations related to the effective implementation of the Conditions.
The ACCC considers that the integrity of the Divestiture Business is appropriately managed, including because the undertaking provides for:

items: obligations on Peter Warren to protect the Divestiture Business prior to divestiture,
the appointment of an ACCC-approved independent manager to manage the Divestiture Business prior to divestiture, and
the appointment of an ACCC-approved independent auditor to monitor and report on compliance with the undertaking.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC also considers that any risk that divestiture will be frustrated, for example, due to third-party consents and renewals, is appropriately managed by the undertaking. 5. Applications for review and public benefit
applications
Applications for review

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s acquisitions register. To confirm whether there has been any application for review, please contact the Australian Competition Tribunal.
Public benefit application

The notifying party may also apply to the ACCC for a determination that the acquisition would be of public benefit. Pursuant to section 51ABZP(2) of the Act, this application must be made no later than 21 calendar days after the ACCC made this determination.
